back2basics.text: Delimitation is the process of redrawing the boundaries of electoral constituencies to reflect changes in population. It ensures fair representation in Parliament by adjusting seat allocation among states based on Census data. The Constitution allows Parliament to amend rules on delimitation, but such changes affect federal balance and political representation.

2026-11-27-am-55d5f02665.deck: The Indian government has called a special Parliament session from November 30 to December 3, 2026, to table and discuss the amended Delimitation Bill. This session is significant for UPSC aspirants as it involves constitutional amendments affecting electoral representation and federal balance.

editor.prelimsAngle: Delimitation Bill and special Parliament session dates.
editor.why: Delimitation Bill impacts electoral representation and federal structure; constitutional significance.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the amended Delimitation Bill and the special Parliament session in 2026:

mcq.trap: A trap could be confusing the Census year used for redrawing constituencies; the Bill uses the 2011 Census, not the 1971 Census, which is only used for proportional strength freeze.

body.label: Session dates and agenda
body.text: Parliament will meet from November 30 to December 3, 2026, to consider the amended Delimitation Bill, which proposes changes to the allocation and redrawing of Lok Sabha seats.

body.label: Bill clearance
body.text: The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on November 27, 2026, to clear the amended legislation before it is tabled in Parliament.

sections.heading: What is the purpose of the special Parliament session?

body.label: Uniform seat increase
body.text: The Bill proposes a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats across states.

body.label: Extension of freeze on seat allocation
body.text: It extends the freeze on using the 1971 Census for determining the proportional strength of states in the Lok Sabha by 25 years.

body.label: Use of 2011 Census for redrawing
body.text: The Bill proposes using the 2011 Census data to redraw constituencies within each state.

body.label: Replication of 2001 amendment
body.text: These changes replicate the formula introduced by the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001.

sections.heading: What are the key changes proposed in the amended Delimitation Bill?

body.label: Impact on state representation
body.text: If the freeze on seat allocation lapses after 2026, states like Tamil Nadu could lose Lok Sabha seats based on new Census data, affecting their political influence.

body.label: Political arithmetic
body.text: The government expects to secure support from various parties to achieve the two-thirds majority needed to pass the Bill.

body.label: Opposition concerns
body.text: Opposition leaders have criticized the timing and intent of the Bill, calling it an assault on the Constitution and democratic processes.

sections.heading: Why does the Delimitation Bill matter for federalism and electoral representation?

body.label: Government alliances
body.text: The NDA is confident of support from allied parties and some breakaway factions, aiming for a two-thirds majority.

body.label: Opposition stance
body.text: Congress and other opposition parties have expressed strong opposition, alleging constitutional violations.

body.label: DMK's position
body.text: DMK has not publicly opposed the Bill yet, with some leaders concerned about potential loss of seats if the freeze is lifted.

sections.heading: How are political parties responding to the Bill?

back2basics.text: The Adjudicating Authority (AA) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) is a quasi-judicial body that decides whether property is proceeds of crime and can be attached or confiscated. It functions through benches composed of judicial, administrative, and financial members. The AA's decisions affect the possession rights of individuals even before conviction, making its composition and legal competence crucial.

2026-11-27-am-707b7ff61e.deck: The Supreme Court ruled that the Adjudicating Authority (AA) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) must include at least one judicial member when deciding on property attachments. This ruling clarifies the legal composition of the AA and emphasizes judicial oversight in anti-money laundering enforcement, relevant for both Prelims and Mains.

editor.mainsAngle: Judicial oversight in anti-money laundering enforcement.
editor.prelimsAngle: PMLA and Supreme Court ruling on bench composition.
editor.why: Clarifies composition of quasi-judicial benches under anti-money laundering law; legal procedural importance.

2026-11-27-am-707b7ff61e.oneLine: The Supreme Court held that PMLA property attachment benches must have at least one judicial member to ensure legal objectivity in adjudication.

faq.a: It adjudicates whether property is proceeds of crime and confirms attachment or restoration.
faq.q: What is the role of the Adjudicating Authority under the PMLA?

faq.a: The bench must have at least one judicial member to ensure legal objectivity.
faq.q: What did the Supreme Court rule about the composition of the PMLA Adjudicating Authority?

faq.a: It centralized the multiple Adjudicating Authorities into a single body.
faq.q: What change did the 2009 amendment make to the Adjudicating Authority under the PMLA?

mains.demand: Explain why judicial members are essential in the PMLA Adjudicating Authority and discuss the implications of the Supreme Court's ruling.
mains.question: Examine the importance of judicial oversight in the adjudication process under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, with reference to the Supreme Court's recent ruling on the composition of the Adjudicating Authority.

body: The PMLA allows attachment of property before conviction, necessitating careful adjudication to protect civil rights.
The Supreme Court ruled that at least one judicial member must be on the bench to interpret law and precedents properly.
The ruling highlights the need for legal competence in decisions affecting property rights and calls for reverting to multiple Adjudicating Authorities to manage workload.
This ensures a balance between effective anti-money laundering enforcement and safeguarding constitutional rights.
structure.conclusion: Judicial presence in the PMLA Adjudicating Authority is vital for fair adjudication and upholding the rule of law.
structure.intro: Judicial oversight ensures legal objectivity and protection of rights in quasi-judicial bodies like the PMLA Adjudicating Authority.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the Adjudicating Authority under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA):

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the 2009 amendment centralized the Adjudicating Authority into a single body, not multiple.

body.label: Judicial member required
body.text: The Supreme Court held that the Adjudicating Authority (AA) under the PMLA must have at least one judicial member on the bench adjudicating property attachment cases.

body.label: Role of the AA
body.text: The AA adjudicates whether a citizen's property is 'proceeds of crime' and confirms attachment, functioning through benches composed of judicial, administrative, and financial members.

body.label: Legal objectivity
body.text: Presence of a judicial member ensures legal objectivity and proper interpretation of law and precedents in decisions involving property attachment.

sections.heading: What is the Supreme Court's ruling on PMLA Adjudicating Authority composition?

body.label: Pre-trial property attachment
body.text: The PMLA permits the State to attach a citizen's property even before guilt is proven, making the AA's role critical in protecting civil rights.

body.label: Substantial consequences
body.text: Adjudication under Section 8 of the PMLA can lead to dispossession of property until trial conclusion, affecting constitutional rights.

body.label: Need for judicial competence
body.text: The court emphasized that adjudication requires a legal mind to ensure fair and lawful decisions on property attachment.

sections.heading: Why does this ruling matter for anti-money laundering enforcement?

body.label: Original multiple AAs
body.text: Originally, the PMLA provided for multiple Adjudicating Authorities, but a 2009 amendment centralized it into a single body.

body.label: Repeal recommendation
body.text: The Supreme Court urged the Union government to consider repealing the 2009 amendment and revert to multiple AAs to handle rising complaints and attachments.

body.label: Workload concerns
body.text: A single AA may be overwhelmed by the increasing number of complaints and provisional attachments each year.

sections.heading: What changes did the Court suggest regarding the PMLA framework?

back2basics.text: A Strategic Defence Partnership is a formal agreement between countries to collaborate on defence-related matters such as joint development, production, training, and technology sharing. It aims to enhance mutual security, promote defence industry growth, and address regional security challenges through cooperation.

This development is important for UPSC aspirants as it highlights India's strategic defence partnerships and focus on defence innovation and technology.

back2basics.concept: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and Food Labelling
back2basics.text: FSSAI is the regulatory body responsible for setting standards and regulating food safety in India. Food labelling provides consumers with information about the nutritional content of packaged foods, helping them make informed choices. Front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) uses clear, visible labels on the front of food packages to indicate high levels of nutrients of concern such as sugar, fat, and salt.

2026-11-27-am-f51883926a.deck: The Supreme Court has mandated the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to implement a single-phase front-of-pack nutrition labelling system with prominent red warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, saturated fat, or salt. This judicial directive highlights the role of the judiciary in public health governance and consumer protection.

editor.mainsAngle: Judiciary's role in public health governance.
editor.prelimsAngle: FSSAI and Supreme Court food labelling directive.
editor.why: Judicial intervention on public health regulation and food safety standards.

2026-11-27-am-f51883926a.oneLine: The Supreme Court ordered FSSAI to finalise stricter front-of-pack nutrition labelling within four months to protect consumers' right to health.

faq.q: What nutrients must FSSAI focus on for the new food labelling norms?

faq.q: What is the deadline set by the Supreme Court for FSSAI to finalise the draft labelling regulations?

mains.demand: Discuss how judicial intervention can influence public health governance and consumer protection using the recent Supreme Court order on food labelling as an example.
mains.question: Examine the role of the judiciary in regulating public health through food safety standards, with reference to the Supreme Court's directive on stricter food labelling norms.

body: The Supreme Court mandated FSSAI to implement stricter front-of-pack nutrition labelling within a fixed timeline to protect consumer health.
The judgment emphasizes the right to health and the state's obligation to regulate harmful industry practices.
It addresses challenges like 'double standards' by multinational companies and the need for clear, effective labelling to inform consumers.
The Court also highlighted the importance of nutritional literacy and safeguards against misuse of transition periods.
structure.conclusion: The Supreme Court's directive exemplifies how judicial oversight can strengthen food safety regulations and promote informed consumer choices.
structure.intro: Judiciary plays a crucial role in upholding public health rights by directing regulatory bodies to enforce safety standards.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's directive on food labelling:
1. The Court instructed FSSAI to treat 'total sugars' and 'saturated fat' as nutrients of concern instead of 'added sugar' and 'added fat'.
2. The Court allowed a transition period of 60 days for food businesses to comply with the new labelling norms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the transition period allowed is 365 days, not 60 days; 60 days is the public comment period for the draft regulations.

body.label: Single-phase labelling regime
body.text: The Court directed FSSAI to formulate a single-phase front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) regime mandating prominent red warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, saturated fat, or salt.

body.label: Nutrients of concern
body.text: FSSAI was asked to treat 'total sugars' and 'saturated fat', rather than 'added sugar' and 'added fat', alongside salt, as the nutrients of concern for labelling.

body.label: Design and size of labels
body.text: The Court prescribed separate red hexagon warning labels for each nutrient with pictorial representation and text such as 'HIGH FAT', 'HIGH SUGAR', or 'HIGH SALT', occupying 4% to 5% of the package's principal display panel.

body.label: Deadline and transition period
body.text: FSSAI must finalise the draft regulations within four months and allow a 365-day transition period for compliance, with safeguards to prevent misuse such as stockpiling unlabelled products.

sections.heading: What did the Supreme Court direct FSSAI to do?

body.label: Right to health obligation
body.text: The Court observed that the right to health obliges the state to regulate industry practices detrimental to public health, including controlling exposure to harmful substances in food.

body.label: Consumer protection
body.text: Mandatory warning labels help consumers make informed choices by clearly indicating high levels of sugar, fat, or salt in packaged foods.

body.label: Preventing label fatigue
body.text: The Court cautioned against setting thresholds too low or too high to avoid desensitising consumers or allowing unhealthy products to escape scrutiny.

body.label: Addressing double standards
body.text: The Court highlighted concerns about multinational food companies applying different standards in India compared to other countries, emphasizing equal protection for Indian consumers.

sections.heading: Why does this matter for public health and consumer rights?

body.label: Nutritional literacy in schools
body.text: The Court emphasized early nutritional education as preventive healthcare and directed the Centre to ensure compliance with existing regulations and enhance school curricula with interactive teaching methods.

body.label: Enforcement safeguards
body.text: FSSAI was instructed to prevent misuse of the transition period by planning how to phase out unlabelled products already in circulation and control excessive manufacturing without labels.

sections.heading: How does the judgment address nutritional literacy and enforcement?
